sources.title: Pavel Etingof, Shlomo Gelaki, Dmitri Nikshych, and Victor Ostrik, Tensor Categories, Mathematical Surveys and Monographs 205 (author-final full text)
sources.locator: Complete 362-page PDF retrieved and inspected. Read Definition 4.1.1; §§7.14–7.15 on doubles and Yetter–Drinfeld modules; and §§8.1–8.3 on braidings, braid-group actions, and coherence, including Exercise 8.2.7.

contents.name: Definition 4.1.1: locally finite linear tensor-category hypotheses
contents.support: The local definition spells out the locally finite linear rigid monoidal hypotheses and End(1)=k condition rather than assuming a fusion or modular category.

source_review.read_extent: The named passage and its complete local argument were inspected in the downloaded full text.
source_review.limitations: No semisimplicity, unitarity, or modularity is added to the local categorical construction.

contents.name: §8.1: braided monoidal categories and the two hexagon identities
contents.support: The local definition uses a natural isomorphism c with both hexagons, then defines each adjacent generator by conjugating the local braiding with associators.

source_review.read_extent: The named passage and its complete local argument were inspected in the downloaded full text.
source_review.supports: The braided-category data and hexagon convention.
source_review.limitations: The local proof invokes the exact imported coherence theorem for equality of composites.

contents.name: §8.2: braid-group action on tensor powers
contents.support: The local proof constructs the Artin-generator assignment and checks adjacent and distant relations using the underlying braid.

source_review.read_extent: The named passage and its complete local argument were inspected in the downloaded full text.
source_review.limitations: No faithfulness of the action is asserted.

contents.name: §7.14: finite quantum-double construction with the book’s H⊗H*cop convention
contents.support: This passage is used as a convention comparison only; the local definition follows the inspected supplier D(H)=H*op⊗H and records its factor order explicitly.

source_review.read_extent: The named passage and its complete local argument were inspected in the downloaded full text.
source_review.supports: A second treatment of finite quantum doubles and their module braiding.
source_review.limitations: The book uses a different factor-order/op-cop convention, so none of its displayed R formulas is substituted into the local statement.

contents.name: Exercise 8.2.7: coherence extension from strict to non-strict parenthesizations
contents.reason: The source leaves the non-strict coherence detail as an exercise; the local proof instead cites the complete imported braided-coherence theorem and proves the generator action from that exact statement.

source_review.read_extent: Complete book PDF downloaded; all listed sections and their displayed hypotheses/conventions were inspected.
source_review.supports: Tensor-category assumptions, braided coherence, braid actions, and an independent quantum-double convention comparison.
source_review.limitations: EGNO’s finite-double convention differs from the exact local finite-double supplier; its quantum-double formula is not used as the local factor-order convention.

sources.title: Samson Black, Representations of Hecke Algebras and the Alexander Polynomial, University of Oregon dissertation (2010)
sources.locator: Complete 58-page dissertation PDF retrieved and inspected. Read §II.2.2 Definition 11.2.3 and §II.3 Definitions 11.3.1, Lemma 11.3.2, Theorems 11.3.3–11.3.4, including the generator rescaling and loop convention.

contents.name: §II.2.2 Definition 11.2.3: type-A Hecke generator relations
contents.support: The local proof derives the quadratic relation and factors through the standard H(q²) presentation after the explicit rescaling T_i=qB_i.

source_review.read_extent: The named passage and its complete local argument were inspected in the downloaded full text.
source_review.limitations: The local proof fixes its own RG-13 parameter v=q² and verifies the rescaling algebraically.

contents.name: §II.3 Definition 11.3.1: Temperley–Lieb generators and loop relations
contents.support: The local theorem assumes exactly the square, adjacent, and distant TL relations and independently expands the braid difference.

source_review.read_extent: The named passage and its complete local argument were inspected in the downloaded full text.
source_review.supports: The TL operator relations and loop parameter.
source_review.limitations: The local theorem accepts these relations conditionally; the source normalization is translated explicitly.

contents.name: §II.3 Theorem 11.3.3: surjective Hecke-to-TL map H_i↦v−U_i
contents.support: The map is an independent quotient comparison; with Black’s symmetric parameter v=q and our normalized generator T_i=qB_i, the quadratic Hecke parameter is v=q², which the local proof checks directly.

source_review.read_extent: The named passage and its complete local argument were inspected in the downloaded full text.
source_review.limitations: The local statement proves a representation on any operator family satisfying TL relations; it makes no Markov-trace or link-invariant claim.

contents.name: §II.3 Theorem 11.3.4: kernel ideal of the universal Hecke-to-TL map
contents.reason: The assigned statement does not identify the universal quotient kernel; it proves the conditional operator representation and its quadratic relation only.

contents.name: §II.2.3 and later chapters: Markov-trace specializations and Alexander/Jones link invariants
contents.reason: No Markov trace, closure evaluation, polynomial link invariant, or empirical braid experiment is asserted by this pair.

source_review.read_extent: Complete dissertation PDF downloaded; §II.2.2 and §II.3 were inspected, including all proof steps of the Hecke-to-TL map and its kernel theorem.
source_review.supports: Hecke and TL presentations, the Hecke-to-TL map, and the source parameter conversion.
